question: Will Ephraim return to Egypt?
summary: Hosea 8:13 and 9:3 announce that Ephraim — the northern kingdom — will return to Egypt as punishment. Hosea 11:5 declares that Ephraim shall not return into the land of Egypt, but rather the Assyrian will be his king. The contradiction is internal to a single prophet, and the prophet doesn't seem to notice the problem.

reconcile.connective: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown quote both verses and resolve the clash via Fairbairn: 'Egypt' names the bondage-state, not the literal country.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible names this a flat contradiction, pairing 'shall return to Egypt' directly against 'shall not return into ... Egypt.'

pd_work.note: Haley's Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies (1874) was checked against its full text and does not treat this Hosea pair, so the row's own harmonizing commentator is used instead: K&D name it outright as 'the apparent contradiction between the words, "It will not return into the land of Egypt," and the threat contained in Hos 8:13; Hos 9:3, that Israel should return to Egypt,' and resolve it by reading Egypt in the earlier threats as 'a type of the land of bondage,' a typology precluded in 11:5 by the explicit contrast with Asshur.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB explicitly names the clash by quoting Hosea 11:5's 'shall not return' directly against Hosea 9:3's return-to-Egypt threat, then resolves it by citing Fairbairn's reading of 'Egypt' as a byword for a bondage-condition Assyria would replicate, not the literal country revisited.
excerpts.source_note_text:
return to Egypt--(See on Hos 8:13). As in Hos 11:5 it is said, "He shall not return into . . . Egypt." FAIRBAIRN thinks it is not the exact country that is meant, but the bondage state with which, from past experience, Egypt was identified in their minds. Assyria was to be a second Egypt to them. Deu 28:68, though threatening a return to Egypt, speaks (Deu 28:36) of their being brought to a nation which neither they nor their fathers had known, showing that it is not the literal Egypt, but a second Egypt-like bondage that is threatened.
eat unclean things in Assyria--reduced by necessity to eat meats pronounced unclean by the Mosaic law (Eze 4:13). See Kg2 17:6.
